questions.question: The Government _____ is a statement of expected receipts and expected expenditures of the Government (for the coming fiscal year) that reveals the budgetary policy of the Government to achieve the twin objective of growth and stability.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Budget**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A government budget is an annual financial statement that outlines estimated government expenditures and expected government receipts or revenues for the forthcoming fiscal year.
 
• In India, it is a constitutional requirement (Article 112) that the government give a statement of estimated income and expenditures to Parliament for each financial year that runs from April 1 to March 31.
 
• This 'Annual Financial Statement' is the government's primary budget document.
 
• Budgets are grouped into three categories based on these estimates:
 
 
• Balanced budget.
 
• Surplus budget.
 
• Deficit budget.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A government budget is said to be a balanced budget if the estimated government expenditures in a given fiscal year are equal to the expected government receipts.

 
 
• A balanced budget ensures economic stability if implemented successfully.
 
• A balanced budget is Inapplicable in less developed countries as it limits the scope of economic growth.
 
 
 
• A government budget is said to be a surplus budget if the expected government revenues exceed the estimated government expenditure in a particular financial year.
 
 
• A country's financial wealth is indicated by a surplus budget.
 
 
 
• If the estimated government expenditure exceeds the expected government revenue in a given fiscal year, the budget is considered to be a deficit budget.
 
 
• A deficit budget is best suited for developing economies, such as India

questions.question: The first five year plan of India was based on ____.

 __
 
• The first Indian prime minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, presented the First Five-Year Plan to the Parliament of India.
 
• The First Five-year Plan was launched in 1951 which mainly focused on the development of the primary sector.
 
• The First Five-Year Plan was based on the **Harrod–Domar model with few modifications.**
 
• The target growth rate was 2.1% annual gross domestic product (GDP) growth; the achieved growth rate was 3.6% the net domestic product went up by 15.
 
• Many irrigation projects were initiated during this period, including the Bhakra, Hirakud, Mettur Dam, and Damodar Valley dams.
 
• At the end of the plan period in 1956, five Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs) were started and The University Grants Commission (UGC) was set up.
 
• Contracts were signed to start five steel plants, which existed in the middle of the Second Five-Year Plan.
 
• The plan was quasi-successful for the government.

Time = Distance / Speed

Relative speed = 90 km/hr - 40 km/hr

Convert speed from km/hr to m/s:

Time taken = Distance / Speed

⇒ Time taken = 625 / (125/9)

⇒ Time taken = 625 × (9/125)

⇒ Time taken = 45 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is option 1.**

Sum of ages of all boys = Average age × Number of boys

New average age = (Sum of ages of remaining boys) / (Number of remaining boys)

**Calculation:**

Initial sum of ages = 21 × 27

Initial sum of ages = 567

New sum of ages (after one boy leaves) = 21.7 × 26

New sum of ages = 21.7 × 26

New sum of ages = 564.2

Age of the boy who left = Initial sum of ages - New sum of ages

Age of the boy who left = 567 - 564.2

Age of the boy who left = 2.8 years

**The correct answer is option 2.**
